selection: Focused convenience pilot; not systematic, representative or class-balanced. Sources located through PubMed/PMC searches on St Johns wort pharmacokinetics and PXR induction.

sources.title: Pharmacokinetic interaction of digoxin with an herbal extract from St John's wort (Hypericum perforatum)
sources.summary: Controlled volunteer study reports reduced digoxin exposure after repeated LI160 administration; the single-dose observation differs. Transporter induction is suggested, not established by this abstract.
sources.caution: Context-dependent study finding; not an independent consensus label.

sources.title: Alterations in cyclosporin A pharmacokinetics and metabolism during treatment with St John's wort in renal transplant patients
sources.summary: Open-label renal-transplant study reports reduced dose-corrected cyclosporin exposure and altered metabolite patterns during supplementation.
sources.caution: Not a blinded trial; clinical context and dose adjustment require full-text review.

sources.title: Gauging the clinical significance of P-glycoprotein-mediated herb-drug interactions: comparative effects of St. John's wort, Echinacea, clarithromycin, and rifampin on digoxin pharmacokinetics
sources.summary: Volunteer comparison reports reduced digoxin exposure with St Johns wort and no detected pharmacokinetic effect with the tested Echinacea regimen.
sources.caution: Also supports review of HERB_ECHINACEA/DRUG_DIGOXIN. Shared publication must remain one provenance component; no detected effect is not universal absence of interaction.

sources.title: St. John's wort induces hepatic drug metabolism through activation of the pregnane X receptor
sources.access_scope: PubMed abstract and indexed PMC full-text excerpts; direct PMC access challenged
sources.location: Abstract; Results CYP3A4 induction; Figure 3 caption
sources.summary: Hyperforin activates PXR; experiments in primary human hepatocytes report increased CYP3A4 expression following hyperforin or extract exposure.
sources.caution: Cellular mechanism evidence, not pair-level clinical ground truth. Do not map receptor binding affinity to CYP inhibition potency or expression to an approved numerical feature without review.
